result.summary: The claim concerns a possible lease termination. The file contains only the tenant’s message: he says the caretaker verbally told him the owner wanted him out by year-end, but he is still waiting for the letter and does not know the dates. He also reports water coming through the bathroom ceiling and two September communications to the landlord requesting a rent reduction. No written termination notice or proof of its receipt is in the file.
result.answer: A formal termination cannot yet be assessed: the tenant is still awaiting the letter. Request the notice, official form, and proof/date of receipt when received. Checklist items also missing: lease; defect notices and delivery proof; dated photos; landlord-response history; humidity/temperature log.
open_points: Whether a formal termination notice has been served remains unresolved; the tenant says he is still waiting for the letter.
The date and proof of receipt are unknown, so the applicable challenge deadline cannot be assessed.

Checklist-listed missing documents: lease contract; defect notice; proof of notification; dated photographs; landlord response history; humidity and temperature log; written termination notice and official form (suggested); and proof/date of service (suggested). Caretaker correspondence is also missing but optional.
The file does not include the communications the tenant says he sent about the water ingress; their exact dates and year are unknown.

reply.subject: Documents concerning the reported termination and water ingress

clauses.text: In your message, you say that you are still waiting for the letter from the office and do not know the relevant dates.

When you receive it, please send us a complete copy of the written termination notice, including any official form served with it, and proof showing when and how you received it; please also tell us the receipt date.
For the water ingress you report in the bathroom ceiling, please send us your lease, the defect notices you sent to the landlord, and proof of delivery or dispatch.
Please also send dated photographs, the landlord’s replies or other communications, and any humidity and temperature log you have; caretaker correspondence about the incident could also help.
